promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 8 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: The key this week is to stick to the planned mileage and not add extra miles to recover lost time.

flags.title: Missing Thursday run
flags.detail: watch to keep weekly volume. Long run HR drift: monitor heat load and keep HR under 150. Easy run HR rising: keep effort moderate to avoid overheating. Training balance: aim for 80% easy running share. Recovery sleep: low hours may affect next week’s performance.

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer: I wouldn’t add extra miles. Stick to the planned 6‑mi easy, the 8‑mi threshold, and the 13‑mi long run. The missed Thursday can be compensated by the upcoming long run, and staying within the weekly total will keep the training load safe and steady.

new.analysis: The athlete ran a week with a missed Thursday easy run and a short long run, dropping about 2‑3 miles of planned mileage. The heart‑rate drift on the long run increased, suggesting the heat may have pushed him harder than expected. His easy‑run HR rose to 151–153, close to his max, so he’s running a bit on the warm side. The rest‑day sleep was low at 5.5 hrs, so recovery could be affected. In the build phase we keep the quality session on Wednesday and the long run on Sunday. We do not add extra mileage to make up for lost weeks; adding extra distance on top of the scheduled volume can increase injury risk and overload the recovery. Instead, keep the week’s mileage in line with the plan, focus on effort and recovery, and slowly raise the easy‑run volume over several weeks.
